data.narrative:
Lumafield, a Series C robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $142M to date, is evaluated against a comparative universe of 9 private peers and 1 public comparable. The private peer set includes stage-adjacent companies such as Exotec (Series D, $2.0B), Bedrock Robotics (Series B, $1.8B), Dexterity (Series B, $1.6B), and Hadrian (Series D, $1.6B), among others in the robotics and manufacturing sector.

Two triangulation methods were applied. The stage-progression method, using $10M as a total-raised proxy and applying a 1.7x Series C step-up multiplier, implies a valuation of $17M. The peer-median method, derived from 7 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables, yields a median valuation of $1.6B with a range of $1.0B to $2.0B. The peer-median result reflects substantial valuations commanded by Series B and Series D robotics companies in the current market.

The triangulated analysis supports a range of $14M to $1.9B, with a median of $834M. This wide range reflects material tension between stage-progression mechanics (which anchor low) and peer-market pricing (which anchors high). Key uncertainties include the maturity and revenue profile of Lumafield relative to the peer set, capital efficiency, and whether near-term financing milestones will track toward Series D or recalibrate stage-progression assumptions.
